newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile backs Canada's expulsion of bogus asylum-seekers.
newsitem.headline: Chile backs Canada's expulsion of bogus asylum-seekers.

text.p: Chile has no objection to plans by Canada to expel about 2,000 Chileans who falsely claimed political asylum, Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza said on Monday, calling their claims of persecution "ridiculous."
Insulza said the thousands of Chileans who streamed into Canada in 1995 and 1996 demanding political asylum so they could stay and work legally in Canada had damaged Chile's international reputation.

Canada, which tightened up visa requirements for Chileans last year in the face of the influx, has already deported "several hundred" Chileans whose asylum claims were deemed bogus and about 2,000 more have their asylum claims still pending, Insulza said.
"The logical thing is to deport them all because they entered Canada under false pretenses. And their pretenses also did visible damage to our country's image," he told reporters.

The only way Chile could avoid the asylum-seekers from returning home, if it wanted to, would be to confirm that they are victims of political persecution, "and that would be ridiculous," said Insulza.

Chilean newspaper El Mercurio reported on Sunday that of 4,300 Chileans who asked for political asylum in Canada, only 50 were accepted while about 1,300 have already been expelled or left voluntarily.

The saga of Chile's bogus asylum-seekers began in 1995 when Canada, just after a visit to Santiago by Prime Minister Jean Chretien, said Chilean passport-holders no longer needed a visa to travel to Canada for short visits.

Within months, Chileans began flying to Canada and asking for political asylum on arrival, despite the fact that Chile has been under civilian democratic rule since 1990. The Chilean asylum-seekers took advantage of Canadian law which allows asylum-seekers to stay in the country and work while their requests are being decided.
By the time Canada reimposed the visa requirement in June last year, about 4,300 Chileans had arrived in Canada requesting asylum and claiming political persecution, Chilean news reports said.
